text:
Zack Ostapchuk was out of the lineup on Nov. 7 in Dallas: Sharks Hockey Digest reported the Sharks inserted a rookie in his place. On a team that had lost four in a row, it's a warning.

His role is clear. He's 6-foot-4, kills penalties, throws hits (44 in 17 games) and plays about 11 minutes a night. His one goal came on Oct. 22 against Ottawa, the team that drafted him 39th overall in 2021. The problem is five on five: the Sharks have had only 35% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, about 10 points worse than without him.

There is a defensive case for him. Evolving-Hockey rated him in the 87th percentile at reducing opponents' chances last season, adjusted for teammates and competition. And there's a hint of scoring left over from junior: 67 points in 55 WHL games with Vancouver in 2022-23. Our numbers see about eight goals over the rest of the season if he plays every night. Getting back in, and staying in, comes first.
headline: Zack Ostapchuk loses his spot as the Sharks slide
